  "text": "Every Thursday, the lighthouse keeper, Mara, carried a thermos of tea to the cliff path and watched the fishing boats return. She had lived on the island for six years, long enough to recognize each boat by its shape and the way it leaned into the wind. But one evening, a small blue sail appeared beyond the reef, moving slowly against the tide.

Mara lowered her binoculars. The boat had no running lights, and no one stood at the helm. She called the harbor on her radio, then hurried down the narrow path toward the cove. By the time she arrived, the boat had drifted close to shore. A boy climbed out, soaked to the waist, clutching a wooden box.

He explained that his grandfather had built the boat years ago and promised to sail it around the island with him. His grandfather had died before they could go. The boy had found the boat in a shed that morning and launched it alone, hoping to fulfill the promise. He had not expected the wind to carry him so far.

Mara wrapped him in her coat and helped him carry the box to the harbor. Inside lay a hand-drawn map of the island, marked with tiny stars. At the bottom, in careful handwriting, was a note: “For our first voyage together.”

The boy stared at the words. Mara poured tea into the thermos cup and sat beside him on the sea wall. They traced the route with a finger, naming the coves and headlands. The voyage had not gone as planned, but the map gave them somewhere to begin again."
